lines.trans: Cindy, how are you feeling—are you okay? I am truly sorry.
It is okay—it is not as if you did it on purpose.
In that split second, my only thought was that I had to save Cindy!
I am sorry I failed to control my own strength.
I can vouch that Senior Ye-jin truly never meant for it to turn out like this.
Please stop apologizing—I do not hold any grudge against you either, Producer.
Thanks to this, it feels like my first real break in ages—for the first time in forever I slept soundly for over three hours.

words.gloss: for the first time in ages

lines.trans: And you, Manager—what were you doing when Cindy had her accident!
What could my manager have done—I got hurt from my own mistake up on my stage.
Our Cindy is so kind-hearted!

What could my manager have done—I got hurt from my own mistake up on my stage.
Our Cindy is so kind-hearted!
See you next time!

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 신디 몸은 어때, 괜찮아요? 정말 미안해.
examples.trans: Cindy, how are you feeling—are you okay? I am truly sorry.
Here the word for 'your body, health' is key.

meanings.en: to be how, to be in what state
meanings.note: Its adverbial form 어떻게 ('how') is used to ask how something is done or how things turned out.

examples.trans: How do you feel today?
How did the meeting turn out?

괜찮다.gloss: to be fine; to be okay

meanings.en: to be fine; to be okay; to be alright
meanings.note: Used to reassure someone, decline an offer politely, or say something is acceptable.

examples.trans: I'm really fine.
Is it okay if we meet tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used to emphasize an adjective or verb.

examples.trans: It's really pretty.
I'm truly sorry.

meanings.en: to be sorry; to feel apologetic
meanings.note: Descriptive adjective; used with peers or younger people (whereas 죄송하다 is honorific/humble).

examples.trans: I'm really sorry I'm late.

examples.text: 미안하지만 다시 한 번 말씀해 주세요.
examples.trans: I'm sorry, but please say that one more time.
I understand well (on purpose).
Today is a (on purpose) busy day.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken intensifier; can also function as a noun meaning 'the real thing'.

examples.trans: I'm really busy today.
Is that really delicious?

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

examples.text: 피디가 마지막 순간까지 잊지 않아야 되는 게 뭔지 알아?
examples.trans: Do you know what a producer must never forget until the very last moment?
The topic of until the moment came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 나는 진짜 그 순간 신디를 구해야겠다 그 생각뿐이었다니까!
examples.trans: In that split second, my only thought was that I had to save Cindy!
This expression comes from 'must save'.

meanings.note: noun thought

examples.trans: Good idea.
Come to mind.

examples.text: 잊지 않고 꼭 갚아 줄 수 있어야 피디한테 힘이 생겨.
examples.trans: Only when people know you remember and repay every debt does a producer gain power.
The topic of power, leverage came up during this shoot.

examples.text: 너무 쉬워도 안 되고 너무 어려워도 안 되니까 조절이 피디의 능력인 거죠.
examples.trans: It cannot be too easy or too hard, so adjusting the level is a producer's skill.
The topic of adjustment, calibration came up during this shoot.

meanings.en: to be unable to, cannot do
meanings.note: Expresses inability; follows a noun in 말 못하다 (cannot say).

examples.trans: I cannot swim.
I couldn't contact you because I was busy.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 내가 힘 조절을 못한 건 미안.
examples.trans: I am sorry I failed to control my own strength.
Here the word for 'sorry' is key.

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.
Did you hear about this to my liking?
I was busy today because of to my liking.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 선배님 마음은 정말 본의 아니게 이렇게 되신 거라는 거 동감합니다.
examples.trans: I can vouch that Senior Ye-jin truly never meant for it to turn out like this.
Here the word for 'original intent' is key.

meanings.note: Adverbial form of 이렇다.
Used to emphasize degree.

examples.trans: You can do it like this.
Why is it so cold today?

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 선배님 마음은 정말 본의 아니게 이렇게 되신 거라는 거 동감합니다.
examples.trans: I can vouch that Senior Ye-jin truly never meant for it to turn out like this.
This expression comes from 'I agree wholeheartedly'.

meanings.note: Often used as a command or suggestion to stop.

examples.trans: Please stop now.
Let's stop fighting.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 그만하세요, 저도 피디님 원망 안 해요.
examples.trans: Please stop apologizing—I do not hold any grudge against you either, Producer.
Here the word for 'resentment, blame' is key.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Usually followed by -e to express gratitude for someone's help.

examples.trans: Thanks to you, I'm doing well.
It is all thanks to the teacher.
Did you hear about this for once, after a while?
I was busy today because of for once, after a while.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 덕분에 간만에 주어진 휴식이랄까, 오랜만에 세 시간 이상 푹 잤어요.
examples.trans: Thanks to this, it feels like my first real break in ages—for the first time in forever I slept soundly for over three hours.
This expression comes from 'given, granted'.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 덕분에 간만에 주어진 휴식이랄까, 오랜만에 세 시간 이상 푹 잤어요.
examples.trans: Thanks to this, it feels like my first real break in ages—for the first time in forever I slept soundly for over three hours.
Here the word for 'call it a break' is key.
Did you hear about this long time no see?
I was busy today because of long time no see.

examples.text: 수습 기간 중에 세 번 사고 치면 잘릴 수도 있대요.
examples.trans: I heard that if you cause trouble three times during probation, you can get fired.
The topic of three came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Available time or duration.
Used with native Korean numbers to count hours (한 시간 = one hour).

examples.trans: Do you have time?
It takes two hours.

meanings.note: Used in negative sentences to mean 'not anymore' or 'no longer'.

examples.trans: I can't do it anymore.
It's beyond expectations.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 여자애들이 우리 승찬이한테 푹 빠져가지고 막 들이대고 그러면,
examples.trans: If those young women fall head over heels for our Seung-chan and throw themselves at him…
Here the word for 'deeply, head over heels' is key.
Did you sleep well last night?
The baby is sleeping right now.

related.gloss: to wake up; to get up

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'manager'

examples.trans: The manager called.
Where is Cindy's manager?
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
Commonly used for traffic or workplace accidents

examples.trans: A big traffic accident happened on the road.

examples.text: 조심하지 않으면 사고가 날 수 있어요.
examples.trans: If you are not careful, an accident can happen.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Kinship term used by females.

meanings.en: older male friend or colleague (used by a female)
meanings.note: Commonly used in Korea to address a close older male acquaintance or coworker.

examples.trans: I have one older brother.
Oppa, do you have time right now?

meanings.note: Interrogative or indefinite pronoun; often shortened to 뭐 in casual speech.

examples.trans: What is your favorite food?
What can I help you with?
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?

meanings.note: physical performance stage
a musical or show performance on stage

examples.trans: We have lots of stages that day.
Today's stage performance was really great.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 편집 잘하면 시련을 당하는 주인공인데 까딱 잘못하면 바보로 보일 수 있다니까!
examples.trans: edited well she is a heroine enduring trials, yet one wrong cut could make her look like a total fool!
This expression comes from 'if it goes wrong'.

다치다.gloss: to get hurt, to be injured

meanings.note: Used for physical injuries

examples.trans: I fell and hurt my knee.
Be careful not to get hurt.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 메이크업이 좀 센 거 같지 않아요? 좀 러블리하고 귀엽고 착해 보이고 그런 거.
examples.trans: Does my makeup not look a bit too fierce? Make it softer—more lovely, cute, and sweet-looking.
This expression comes from 'sweet, gentle'.

meanings.en: what to do, how to act
meanings.note: Contraction of 어떻게 하다.

examples.trans: What should we do?
What should we do? (2)

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
